title: Model Compilation: torch.compile, ONNX & TensorRT
interviewAnswer: Model compilation captures/lowers computation into optimized kernels or runtimes. torch.compile optimizes PyTorch graphs; ONNX enables portable graph runtimes; TensorRT targets NVIDIA inference. I use them only after profiling and verifying numerical/shape compatibility.
why: Compilation can remove Python overhead and fuse operations, but dynamic control flow or unsupported ops can erase the benefit.
intuition: Instead of executing many tiny operations one by one, a compiler sees a larger graph and can combine/reorder work for the target hardware.
deepDive: Compilation has startup/warmup costs and can create graph breaks. Export formats may lose unsupported behaviors. Validate outputs across representative shapes and precision modes.
workedExample: A fixed-shape vision service may gain substantially from TensorRT; a highly dynamic research model may spend more time compiling than it saves.
commonMistakes: Benchmarking the first compiled call and calling it slow.
Assuming ONNX conversion guarantees identical behavior.
followUps: When would you choose ONNX Runtime over TensorRT?
production: Precompile common shapes where possible, cache artifacts, and keep fallback paths for unsupported inputs.
